title: Creamy Homemade Pumpkin Soup
excerpt: When the evenings turn crisp and the porch fills with golden leaves, a warm pot of pumpkin soup feels like a little bowl of home. This creamy, garlicky recipe is simple enough for a weeknight and special enough for a cozy Halloween dinner, just like something Grandma would ladle into waiting bowls.

Why You'll Love This Pumpkin Soup

  • This pumpkin soup is creamy, cozy, and full of gentle autumn flavor.
  • It comes together in one pot with simple pantry-friendly ingredients.
  • Garlic, nutmeg, and maple syrup add a warm, balanced flavor without overpowering the pumpkin.
  • An immersion blender makes the soup smooth with very little fuss.
  • It is a comforting vegetarian dinner for crisp evenings and family gatherings.

Ingredients

Gather these simple ingredients for a silky pumpkin soup that tastes like it simmered all afternoon in Grandma's kitchen.

  • Olive oil - 2 tablespoons
  • Yellow onion - 1 medium, finely chopped
  • Garlic cloves - 3, minced
  • Pumpkin puree - 4 cups
  • Low-sodium vegetable broth - 4 cups
  • Maple syrup - 1 teaspoon
  • Ground nutmeg - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Kosher salt - 1 teaspoon
  • Black pepper - 1/4 teaspoon
  • Heavy cream or full-fat coconut milk - 1 cup
  • Fresh parsley - 2 tablespoons chopped, for serving

How to Make Pumpkin Soup

Set aside 15 minutes for prep and 30 minutes for cooking. There is no extra resting time, so this comforting pumpkin soup can go from the stovetop to the table in about 45 minutes.

Step 1: Warm the Oil

Warm the olive oil in a large soup pot over medium heat. Give the oil a moment to heat gently, but do not let it smoke.

Step 2: Add the Onion

Add the finely chopped onion to the pot. Stir it through the olive oil so the pieces begin to soften evenly.

Step 3: Soften the Onion

Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it is soft and translucent. This gentle start builds a sweet, savory base for the soup.

Step 4: Stir in Garlic

Stir in the minced garlic. Spread it through the softened onion so every spoonful gets a little garlicky goodness.

Step 5: Cook the Garlic

Cook the garlic for 1 minute, stirring often. Stop when it smells fragrant so it does not scorch.

Step 6: Add the Soup Ingredients

Add the pumpkin puree, vegetable broth, maple syrup, nutmeg, salt, and black pepper. Stir well to combine the ingredients into a smooth, seasoned mixture.

Step 7: Bring to a Simmer

Bring the soup to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Keep the heat moderate and stir occasionally as the flavors begin to come together.

Step 8: Simmer the Soup

Simmer the soup for 20 minutes. This gives the pumpkin, onion, garlic, and spices time to make a warm and flavorful broth.

Step 9: Remove from Heat

Remove the pot from the heat before blending. Letting the bubbling settle helps make blending more comfortable and controlled.

Step 10: Blend Until Smooth

Blend the soup with an immersion blender until smooth. Move the blender through the pot carefully until no large pieces remain.

Step 11: Stir in the Cream

Stir in the heavy cream or full-fat coconut milk. Mix gently until the soup is creamy and evenly blended.

Step 12: Garnish and Serve

Garnish each serving with fresh parsley. Ladle the soup into bowls and serve while warm.

Pro Tips for Making Pumpkin Soup

  • Use plain pumpkin puree rather than pumpkin pie filling, which contains added sugar and spices.
  • Chop the onion evenly so it softens at the same rate.
  • Keep the soup at a gentle simmer instead of a hard boil to protect its smooth texture.
  • If using coconut milk, stir the can well before measuring for a creamy result.
  • Taste the soup after blending and adjust the salt or pepper if needed.

How to Serve Pumpkin Soup

  • Serve each bowl with a little chopped parsley for a fresh, colorful finish.
  • Pair the soup with warm crusty bread, dinner rolls, or toasted garlic bread.
  • Add a simple green salad for a light and balanced dinner.
  • For a festive meal, serve small bowls as a cozy first course before the main dish.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Cool leftover soup promptly, then place it in a covered container and refrigerate within 2 hours.
  • Store the soup in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.
  • Keep garnishes separate when possible so the parsley stays fresh.

Freezing

  • Freeze cooled soup in freezer-safe containers, leaving room for expansion.
  • For the smoothest texture, freeze the soup before adding the cream or coconut milk, then stir it in after reheating.
  • Thaw frozen soup overnight in the refrigerator before warming.

Reheating

  • Reheat the soup gently in a pot over medium-low heat, stirring often.
  • Do not let the soup boil hard after adding the cream or coconut milk.
  • If the soup thickens in storage, stir in a small splash of vegetable broth until it reaches your preferred consistency.

Final Thoughts

This creamy pumpkin soup is a simple, comforting bowl of autumn goodness that deserves a place in your family recipe collection.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for making and serving this cozy pumpkin soup.

Can I use homemade pumpkin puree?

Yes, homemade pumpkin puree works well as long as it is smooth and not too watery. If it is loose, simmer the soup a little longer to reach a creamy consistency.

Can I make pumpkin soup without heavy cream?

Yes, use full-fat coconut milk instead of heavy cream. It makes the soup creamy while adding a subtle coconut flavor.

Can I make this pumpkin soup ahead of time?

Yes, prepare the soup up to 4 days ahead and store it covered in the refrigerator. Reheat it gently and stir well before serving.

What can I serve with pumpkin soup?

Crusty bread, toasted garlic bread, a green salad, or a simple sandwich all pair nicely with this warm and creamy soup.
